formulas.assumptions: Weights are UX estimates chosen for explainability. They do NOT predict open rates.

checks.basis: estimate — truncation thresholds, not measured open-rate data
checks.rule: +10 if 30–50 chars; +5 if 20–70 chars; −15 if >70 chars; −5 if <15 chars
−12 per ALL-CAPS word; −10 if ≥2 '!' or '$' hype patterns; −8 per bundled trigger phrase

formulas.formula: score = clamp(0, 100, 50 + Σ bonuses − Σ penalties)
formulas.honestyNote: MUST be labeled in UI: 'heuristic estimate, not a prediction'. Never show 'predicted open rate %'.
formulas.name: Subject Line Heuristic Score

formulas.assumptions: Matching is lexical against a bundled curated list; it models common trigger-pattern guidance, not any provider's filter.
formulas.formula: riskScore = Σ (severityWeight(term) × occurrences(term)); riskLevel = low if <3, medium if 3–9, high if ≥10
formulas.honestyNote: This is a pattern linter, NOT a spam-filter test. Real inbox placement depends on sender reputation, authentication, engagement — none testable client-side. UI must say so.
formulas.name: Spam Trigger Match Score

variables.occurrences: case-insensitive whole-word / whole-phrase matches in pasted text
variables.severityWeight: 1 (mild, e.g. 'free trial') | 2 (medium, e.g. 'guaranteed') | 3 (severe, e.g. 'no credit check')

formulas.assumptions: Truncation thresholds come from RULE-EMAIL-009 (commonly-cited guidance). Emoji/double-width glyphs may occupy more visual space than one 'character'.
formulas.formula: charCount = [...subjectLine].length (Unicode code points); wordCount = tokens split on whitespace
formulas.honestyNote: Counting is exact; whether a client truncates at exactly N chars is guidance, not a guarantee.
formulas.name: Subject Line Character Measurement

formulas.assumptions: Even spacing default; user can override per-email offsets. No engagement-based timing (no data client-side).
formulas.formula: gapDays = floor(spanDays / max(emailCount − 1, 1)); date_i = startDate + i × gapDays (i = 0..emailCount−1)
formulas.honestyNote: Scheduling math only — not an optimized send-time recommendation.
formulas.name: Sequence Cadence Spacing

formulas.assumptions: Linear model. Assumes every open is a billable impression and fill rate is 100% unless the user discounts CPM to compensate.
formulas.formula: impressionsPerIssue = subscribers × (openRatePct / 100); revenuePerIssue = impressionsPerIssue × CPM / 1000; revenuePerMonth = revenuePerIssue × issuesPerMonth; revenuePerSubscriberPerMonth = revenuePerMonth / max(subscribers, 1)
formulas.honestyNote: USER-ASSUMPTION-DRIVEN. The formula does not know real CPMs or open rates. Any pre-filled example values must be labeled 'example — enter your own numbers'.
formulas.name: Newsletter Sponsorship Revenue (CPM)

variables.CPM: user-supplied cost per mille in account currency

formulas.assumptions: Greedy wrap (not Knuth-Plass); long URLs/words that exceed lineWidth are hard-broken.
formulas.formula: greedy word-wrap: lines broken at last space ≤ lineWidth; links rendered as 'anchor text <URL>' (inline) or 'anchor text [n]' with footnote list (footnote mode)
formulas.honestyNote: Deterministic transformation — no judgment calls, output is fully reproducible.
formulas.name: Plain-Text Line Wrapping

formulas.assumptions: 'Best' bands (e.g. Tue–Thu mornings) are commonly-cited guidance, labeled with source — not measured facts. Conversion math itself is exact.
formulas.formula: audienceLocal = senderLocal + (audienceOffset − senderOffset), using IANA offsets for the send date (DST-aware via Intl API)
formulas.honestyNote: UI must separate the exact math (timezone conversion) from the guidance (best-time bands).
formulas.name: Send-Time Timezone Conversion

variables.audienceOffset: UTC offset of audience tz on date
variables.senderOffset: UTC offset of sender tz on date

formulas.assumptions: Even distribution; pillar assignment round-robins through the mix. No performance-based scheduling.
formulas.formula: sendDates = evenly spaced startDate..startDate+89d honoring emailsPerWeek and blackoutDates; pillar_i counts = round(total × goalMix_i)
formulas.honestyNote: Calendar math only — the mix is the user's strategy, not a recommendation.
formulas.name: 90-Day Calendar Distribution

formulas.assumptions: Prices and fill rates are user estimates; slots independent.
formulas.formula: grossPerIssue = Σ slot.pricePerIssue; expectedPerIssue = Σ (slot.pricePerIssue × slot.fillRatePct / 100); grossMonthly = grossPerIssue × issuesPerMonth; expectedMonthly = expectedPerIssue × issuesPerMonth; utilization = soldSlots / totalSlots × 100
formulas.honestyNote: USER-ASSUMPTION-DRIVEN. Tool must not display market rate benchmarks as facts. If example slot prices are pre-filled, label them examples.
formulas.name: Newsletter Ad Slot Revenue

honestyPreamble: Every formula here is pure client-side arithmetic on user-supplied inputs. No formula invents market data: CPMs, open rates, 'best times', and scoring weights are USER ASSUMPTIONS or LABELED ESTIMATES. Any default must be shown to the user as an example value, never as a market fact.
